title: Dual-region streaming quiesce and circuit guardrails for hosted API gateway
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Summary: Add a set of coordinated guardrails to the hosted API gateway to enable dual-region failover without dropping live streaming sessions. This ticket defines the quiesce window semantics, circuit-breaker hysteresis, telemetry-driven load-shedding thresholds, and the protocol for stream resumption tokens exchanged between regions.

Background: We operate active deployments in multiple regions. Planned and unplanned regional evacuations must preserve in-flight streaming sessions (HTTP/2 and WebSocket) where possible and gracefully degrade when not. Current behavior either drops streams immediately during a regional pivot or attempts aggressive retries that violate SLOs and exhaust downstream capacities. This effort focuses on deterministic, observable behavior that prioritizes SLO adherence and bounded customer impact.
acceptance_criteria:
1) During a planned region quiesce, at least 95% of streaming sessions are offered a resumption token and remain resumable after failover.
2) For unplanned failover, failover controller will maintain 99.95% region-to-region control-plane reachability decisioning and trigger stage-based circuit breakers.
3) Circuit breaker prevents >90% of overloaded routing attempts toward saturated model pools.
4) Load-shedding triggers documented and visible in Console (per-route shedding metrics) and reduces token cost per second by >=25% under extreme load compared to current baseline.
5) Automated chaos test (simulated region loss) passes with no more than 3%s error-budget burn for critical customers in testbed environment.
design_notes:
- Quiesce window: soft-quiesce (60s) allowing existing in-flight token streams to drain naturally with a hard cutover grace of 10s for long-polling requests.
- Resumption token: opaque signed token containing minimal session metadata (session id hash, last-acknowledged-offset, region-version) with TTL=5 minutes. Tokens are short-lived to limit cross-region replay surfaces.
- Circuit breaker: multi-level with separate health dimensions: (a) EH: egress queue depth, (b) GPU util (90% threshold), (c) model-latency p99 drift > 2x baseline. Each dimension has hysteresis window 30s on, 60s off to avoid flapping.
- Load-shedding policy: tiered: (1) admission-level rejects for unauthenticated/low-tier requests; (2) approximate prefix-caching fast-path for repeated prefixes; (3) token-limited streaming for low-tier sessions (max concurrent tokens/time).
- KV cache reconciliation: streaming checkpoints persisted to regional durable cache with cross-region async replication and a reconciliation job to accept the newest sequence number during resumption.
- Observability: add per-session lifecycle events to Kafka (quiesce-offer,resume-accept,resume-fail,hard-cutover) and Console dashboards for shed-rate, resume-success-rate, and circuit-breaker transitions.
implementation_plan:
1) API: add /v1/streams/resume-token endpoint and token verification helpers in auth layer.
2) Runtime: implement soft-quiesce state machine in edge proxy and propagate quiesce headers to serving plane.
3) Orchestration: extend failover controller to emit stage-based directives (announce-quiesce, enforce-handoff, hard-cutover).
4) Telemetry: instrument metrics and add Grafana panels and Alerting rules for shed-rate > 1% sustained or resume-success-rate < 90%.
5) Testing: unit tests, integration test with synthetic streaming workload, staged canary in one customer cluster, and chaos simulation for region loss.
6) Rollout: start with low-traffic region pair, monitor 48h, then widen to GA.
risks:
- Cross-region resumption token misuse: mitigated by short TTL and signed tokens.
- Increased control-plane load during large-scale quiesce announcements: mitigate by batching directives and rate-limiting telemetry shards.
- KV cache divergence causing resume mismatch: include last-known-offset and optimistic overwrite rule to prefer higher sequence numbers.
- Edge flapping due to aggressive hysteresis misconfiguration: conservative defaults chosen and will be tuned via canary.
- Regulatory concerns for cross-region state transfer: optional opt-out for customers on Private deployments; default behavior is to avoid cross-region materialization for sensitive data.
metrics_and_slos:
- Hosted API target availability during normal ops: 99.95% overall.
- Streaming session preservation SLO: 95% resumable after planned quiesce; 85% after unplanned failover (short).
- Latency SLO: generation p50 < 100ms, p95 < 220ms, p99 < 350ms for non-streaming requests.
- Circuit breaker effectiveness: reduce attempts toward saturated pools by >=90% within 60s of trigger.
- Shed-rate target under overload: keep error budget burn under 3% for critical customers; report shed-rate and price-tier impact in Console.
